01 Antidepressants · class card

SSRIs

selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors · citalopram · escitalopram · fluoxetine · fluvoxamine · paroxetine · sertraline

Key point
  • Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs): block serotonin reuptake early nausea, headache, insomnia, anxiety; later sexual dysfunction, weight gain
  • Class risks: suicidal thoughts under 25 (boxed warning), hyponatremia, and bleeding with an anti-inflammatory or an anticoagulant
  • Citalopram: dose-dependent QT prolongation; avoided after a recent heart attack
  • Paroxetine: the most interactions; first-trimester heart-defect signal
  • Fluoxetine: long half-life no taper
Drugs

Citalopram Celexa: dose-dependent QT prolongation, fewest interactions

Escitalopram Lexapro: few interactions

Fluoxetine Prozac: long half-life no taper needed; strong cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6) inhibitor

Fluvoxamine: strong cytochrome P450 1A2 (CYP1A2) inhibitor

Paroxetine Paxil: most interactions, most discontinuation symptoms, anticholinergic

Sertraline Zoloft: few interactions

Mechanism

more serotonin in the synapse longer postsynaptic stimulation SSRI effects by serotonin (5-HT) receptorType 1 (5-HT1): antidepressant, anti-anxiety effectType 2 (5-HT2): anxiety, insomnia, sexual dysfunctionType 3 (5-HT3): nausea, headacheDopamine, norepinephrine: barely touched

Few anticholinergic or cardiac conduction effects wide safety margin; isolated overdose is usually well tolerated, except with citalopram

Uses

Depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder, premenstrual dysphoric disorder

Fluoxetine: also used for bulimia nervosa

Premature ejaculation: also treated with SSRIs

Menopausal hot flashes: paroxetine, citalopram

Adverse effects

Early: nausea, headache, insomnia or sleepiness, anxiety, dizziness Other common adverse effects (sertraline)Diarrhea, tremor, indigestion, less appetite, sweating

Later: in up to half, weight gain SSRI sexual dysfunctionIn practice: sexual dysfunction in more than half of patientsMost common type: difficulty reaching orgasm

Hyponatremia, often from the , higher risk over 65 Drug causes of SIADHMnemonic: "Can't Concentrate Serum Na+"CarbamazepineCyclophosphamideSSRIsNonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

Paroxetine: anticholinergic; fluoxetine: agitation, early appetite loss

Abrupt stop of a short half-life SSRI such as paroxetine: flu-like, neurologic and psychiatric symptoms within days

Discontinuation syndrome after stopping sertraline or paroxetine: headache, aches, diarrhea, anxiety, fine tremor

Paroxetine stopped abruptly 2 weeks ago: dizziness worse with head movement, paresthesias

Discontinuation syndrome: can mimic influenza, migraine, an anxiety disorder, benign positional vertigo

Paresthesias: absent in benign positional vertigo

Monitoring

Before starting: screen for bipolar disorder

Older adults: serum sodium

QT prolongation on citalopramDose-dependent; maximum 40 mg a day, 20 mg over age 60 or with hepatic impairment Citalopram QT precautionsAvoid in: congenital long QT syndrome, bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, uncompensated heart failureAvoid with: other QT-prolonging drugsMonitor: potassium, magnesium in patients at risk of low levels

If a patient with a recent heart attack needs an SSRI, choose sertraline or escitalopram.

A citalopram overdose can still bring torsade de pointes, and it may be delayed: keep the heart monitored

Suicidal thoughts under 25Boxed warning: more suicidal thoughts in children and adults under 25 in short-term studies

If a patient of any age starts an antidepressant, choose a close watch for worsening mood and suicidal thinking.

Paroxetine in pregnancyFirst-trimester exposure: ↑ risk of cardiac malformations (less than double baseline)

If an SSRI is needed in pregnancy, choose sertraline or escitalopram over paroxetine.

Late-pregnancy SSRI exposureAny SSRI in late pregnancy ↑ risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newbornLate third-trimester exposure some newborns need prolonged hospitalization, respiratory support, tube feeding

Drug interactions
DrugEffectManagement
Monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), current or within the washout period Serotonin syndrome, potentially life-threateningContraindicated
Tramadol, linezolid, triptans, dextromethorphan, ondansetron, St John's wortSerotonin syndrome Monitor for clonus, hyperreflexia; avoid St John's wort
Aspirin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), warfarin, other anticoagulants, including GI bleeding Mechanism of SSRI-associated bleedingSSRI → ↓ platelet serotonin uptakePlatelets need serotonin for hemostasisCounsel on bleeding
Warfarin: check the international normalized ratio (INR)
Tamoxifen, with paroxetine or fluoxetineLess active tamoxifen metabolite (CYP2D6)Choose one with little CYP2D6 inhibition
Tricyclic antidepressants or metoprolol, with paroxetine or fluoxetineTheir levels can rise (CYP2D6)Lower their dose if needed
Tizanidine, ramelteon, theophylline, clozapine, with fluvoxamineTheir levels can rise (CYP1A2)Never combine: tizanidine, ramelteon
Theophylline: reduce to a third of its dose; monitor levels

Practice
  1. 61-year-old man, 3 weeks after an anterior myocardial infarction low mood, anhedonia and poor sleep for a month; wants a medicine takes aspirin, metoprolol and a statin electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm, corrected QT at the upper limit of normal → Citalopram → its dose-dependent QT prolongation makes it the SSRI to avoid after a recent myocardial infarction; sertraline and escitalopram are the first choices, with few drug interactions
  2. 46-year-old woman takes tamoxifen after surgery for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer two months of low mood, poor sleep and guilt meets criteria for major depressive disorder; an SSRI is planned no other medicines → Paroxetine → a strong inhibitor of cytochrome P450 2D6, it lowers the active metabolite of tamoxifen; citalopram inhibits that enzyme only weakly, and escitalopram has few drug interactions
  3. 34-year-old woman started sertraline for major depressive disorder 2 weeks ago on a full dose since; sleep a little better, mood unchanged mild nausea in the first days, now gone no suicidal thoughts → Continue sertraline at the same dose → response usually starts at 2 to 3 weeks and can take up to 8; an adequate trial is at least 4 to 6 weeks at a therapeutic dose, and an abrupt stop can bring discontinuation symptoms
